newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: CRICKET-MOODY FRUSTRATES QUEENSLAND VICTORY PUSH.
newsitem.headline: CRICKET-MOODY FRUSTRATES QUEENSLAND VICTORY PUSH.

text.p: Queensland took an iron grip on the Sheffield Shield final on Monday before Western Australia captain Tom Moody delayed their seemingly inevitable charge to victory with an unbeaten half-century.
Chasing a daunting target of 465 to win, Western Australia were reduced to 18 for four before Moody helped lift his team to 166 for five at close of play on the fourth day at the WACA Ground.
With one day remaining and their last two recognised batsmen at the crease, Western Australia need a further 299 runs to win, with Moody on 66 alongside wicket-keeper Adam Gilchrist on 36 not out.
More realistically, they face the challenge of needing to survive three sessions on Tuesday to claim a draw, which would be sufficient for them to win the Shield.
Under competition rules, Western Australia need only avoid defeat to win the title as a reward for finishing at the top of the table at the end of the regular season.
Queensland fast bowler Adam Dale, who took six wickets in the first innings, struck again to remove openers Mike Hussey and Ryan Campbell cheaply.
Queensland, who scored 320 in their first innings before dismissing their opponents for 165, were all out for 309 on Monday after resuming on 259 for six.

Veteran opener Trevor Barsby, who has scored a century and a half-century in the match, made another crucial contribution in his last appearance before retirement when he took a remarkable reflex catch at short leg to dismiss Campbell.
